findings.body: `hostedAuthorityReference()` now returns either a commit SHA (event-main) or the ref string `refs/heads/main` (remote-main for non-main PR bases). That’s a concrete return-type change that can break callers that assume a 40-hex commit ID (the old behavior enforced that). Options: (1) update the API to return a structured object (e.g., `{ source, reference }`) and migrate internal callers, or (2) keep `hostedAuthorityReference()` returning a commit SHA only (resolve/fetch main inside the function) and introduce a new helper for the “selector ref” behavior.
findings.validation_summary: Actual exported helper has only retained test consumers. Production uses structured hostedContext and resolves authority SHA. Current selector test passes. Compare existing A03 hosted-audit-decision M98 before final disposition.

findings.body: `remove()` can fail on platforms where `os.tmpdir()` is a symlinked path (common on macOS, e.g. `/var` vs `/private/var`). `mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), ...))` will use the non-realpath form, so `path.dirname(root)` may not equal `fs.realpathSync(os.tmpdir())` even though the directory is correct. Compare realpaths on both sides (e.g., `fs.realpathSync(path.dirname(root))`) or use `path.resolve()` consistently to keep this portability check from failing on non-Linux environments.
findings.validation_summary: Real Windows junction proves lexical parent versus realpath mismatch. Both realpaths compare equal. No recursive cleanup performed by reproduction; repair now published and validated; original reproduction retained.
findings.selection: Canonical parent comparison at all six identical test-fixture assertions across three existing test files; preserve names/guards; actual ordinary and linked TEMP validation.

findings.body: `strings[input.filePath] = input.content;` silently overwrites if the same `filePath` appears multiple times in `markdownInputs`, which can hide lint failures for the overwritten content. Consider rejecting duplicates explicitly (throw with a clear tooling-failure message) or normalizing inputs so each path is guaranteed unique before building the `strings` object.
findings.validation_summary: Actual shared API returns0 for invalid then clean content with identical file label; reverse order returns1. No duplicate input demonstrated from current Git/glob production callers. Full decision required.
findings.selection: Reject conflicting exact labels before lint; accept identical content repeats; retain unique-label behavior. Full table displayed, totals verified including F41.

findings.body: The hook no longer provides a targeted “tooling not installed” message (previously it told users to run `node .github/workflows/NpmTools.mjs install`). Consider restoring a lightweight preflight check (e.g., verify `.github/workflows/node_modules` exists or that the required packages can be resolved) and printing a single actionable remediation line before exiting with status 1/2.

findings.body: The outer-lint wrapper describes a bounded execution (notably a two-minute deadline and output limit), but the child invocation here relies on `runBounded` defaults via `run` and doesn’t set explicit `timeout`/`maxBuffer` bounds. Consider passing explicit `timeout` and `maxBuffer` values for this specific child run to keep the bound stable and aligned with the documented contract.

findings.title: Historical setup runtime tuple constants
findings.body: This setup flow embeds specific historical Node/npm versions (`11.16.0`, `24.18.0`, `24.18.1`) directly in the workflow logic. Even if intentional for a “pre-declaration tuple” compatibility path, it creates a high-churn spot on future version bumps and increases the chance of updating one location but missing others (the same versions also appear elsewhere in this workflow). Consider centralizing these tuples into a single well-named data block (within the script) or deriving them from a single authoritative repo file when possible, so future maintenance is less error-prone.

findings.title: Imported lint dependency failure boundary
findings.body: When this module is imported (e.g., by `lint-staged-markdown.mjs`) and a dependency is missing, the code re-throws the raw `require()` error without the `Markdown lint tooling:` prefix and without enforcing a consistent “tooling failure” classification at the boundary. To keep diagnostics stable across direct vs imported execution, consider wrapping/rethrowing with a consistent message (and optionally attaching the original error as `cause`) so callers don’t emit confusing bare loader errors.

native_disposition.reply_body:

findings.title: Windows lint selector path normalization
findings.body: `assertLintConfigurationInputs()` normalizes discovered paths using `relative.split(path.sep).join('/')`. If `globSync()` yields POSIX-style `/` separators on Windows (a common behavior for glob libraries), `path.sep` is `\\` and the normalization becomes a no-op, which can cause allowed configs (like `.github/workflows/.markdownlint.jsonc`) to be incorrectly rejected as “unsupported”. Consider normalizing with a separator-agnostic replacement (e.g., replace backslashes with `/` regardless of platform) or using `path.posix` consistently for comparisons.
findings.head: dde2b9abe761af69a7f561512df7d44d0dec6745

native_disposition.reply_body:
No change: a POSIX path remains equal to the POSIX allowlist when normalization is a no-op. Actual Windows backslash output and Linux POSIX output both pass; an additional Windows real-glob posix:true projection accepts both supported files and still rejects unsupported configurations.
[Decision and evidence](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/f6d66b8f7176b3fe71bb73bf4209e22a5c540bb2/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A07/TF66-R16-posix-path-allowlist.md)
